portfolio.title: Operator kill in <=2 seconds: in-flight subprocess cancel watcher + stderr drain deadlock fix
portfolio.problem: notifications/commands.py promises 'Kill signal sent — the current Claude attempt will be terminated', but nothing watches the ControlBus while the subprocess runs. VERIFIED: agents/executor.py:246-262 consults cancel_check only in the between-attempt rate-limit retry loop; agents/executor_stream.py then blocks in proc.communicate(timeout) or _drainStreaming's 'for line in proc.stdout' (line 200) with only a timeout Timer. !abort/!kill latency is therefore up to the full CLAUDE_CLI_TIMEOUT (600s) — the single worst controllability gap in the system. Separately VERIFIED: _drainStreaming reads stdout to EOF before touching stderr (line 209), so a stderr-chatty child fills the OS pipe buffer, blocks, stdout never EOFs, and the attempt silently burns the entire timeout before tree-kill.
portfolio.design: (1) executor_stream.runSubprocess gains cancel_check: Optional[Callable[[], bool]] = None. One daemon watcher thread: while proc.poll() is None: if cancel_check(): _killProcessTree(proc.pid); cancelled=True; break; sleep(CANCEL_POLL_SECONDS=2.0). On cancelled, return a result with subtype='operator_killed' (distinct from 'timeout'). (2) executor.runClaude threads its existing cancel_check param into runSubprocess on both the communicate and streaming paths. (3) platform_core/orchestration/execute_mixin.py: on subtype=='operator_killed', do NOT count the attempt against MAX_SUBTASK_ATTEMPTS and do not synthesize failure feedback — go straight to the existing _checkControl kill/abort branch, which now fires within seconds instead of after timeout. (4) Fix the drain deadlock: a second daemon thread reads proc.stderr concurrently with the stdout loop; join both before proc.wait(). (5) CANCEL_POLL_SECONDS added to platform_core/app_config/llm.py; commands.py kill message becomes truthful.
portfolio.test_strategy: Unit: fake Popen double that never exits + cancel_check flipping True after 0.1s -> killed within 3s, subtype=='operator_killed'. Deadlock regression: real subprocess ('python -c') writing 1MB to stderr then exiting -> completes in <5s. Integration: extend test_granular_controls.py — requestKillSubprocess mid-attempt terminates the attempt without burning an attempt slot.
portfolio.breaking_changes: Result dicts gain subtype 'operator_killed'; existing 'timeout' semantics unchanged.

portfolio.title: Guard layer actually registered and fail-closed: one risk taxonomy, generated hooks block, dual enforcement kept

VERIFIED: .claude/settings.json has hooks={} (nothing registered); hooks.py:142-149 last-resort handler exits 0 for ALL hooks including guards; hooks_destructive.py:37-38 'except Exception: sys.exit(0)' with classifyActionRisk (line 45) running OUTSIDE any try — a classifier crash falls through to the exit-0 catch-all. The destructive policy is encoded in divergent copies (executor_env command regexes, hooks_selfmod write-command regexes) although hooks_destructive already consumes action_risk.classifyActionRisk — so the dedup is smaller than lens B claimed. CRITICAL nuance verified at executor_env.py:126-127: headless 'claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions' may not run .claude hooks at all, which is exactly why the regex pre-scan exists — so lens B's plan to delete it is WRONG; the fix is one taxonomy feeding both enforcement layers.
portfolio.design: (1) One taxonomy: platform_core/runtime/action_risk.py absorbs executor_env's command-position regexes and hooks_selfmod's write-command regexes as anchored regexes with sudo/chained-command handling; executor_env and hooks_selfmod import it — pattern SOURCE deduped, both enforcement points KEPT (defense in depth given the headless-mode uncertainty). (3) Fail closed: blockDestructive wraps parse+classify in try/except and exits 2 whenever a non-empty Bash command is present but classification crashed; hooks.py main's last-resort handler exits 2 when hook_name is in GUARD_HOOKS={'block_destructive','self_modification_guard'}, 0 otherwise (telemetry hooks stay non-blocking per orchestration rules). (4) Hook context via one env var NINE_TO_FIVE_HOOK_CTX (JSON: boundaries, log path from config.LOG_PATH — delete the hardcoded C:\9to5\logs\hooks.log) so the guard entrypoint imports stdlib + action_risk only. (5) Discord alert moves AFTER the exit decision and becomes fire-and-forget: append one line to logs/guard_alerts.jsonl; the gateway bot tails and posts — no network I/O in the block path.
portfolio.test_strategy: Table-driven taxonomy tests (destructive / safe / prose-containing-'del /s') proving the substring false-positive class is gone; subprocess tests invoking 'python agents/hooks.py block_destructive' with (a) destructive payload -> rc 2, (b) safe -> rc 0, (c) MALFORMED JSON -> rc 2 (fail-closed regression); executor_env test asserting the generated settings JSON always contains the hooks block; health-check test. portfolio.title: Control plane v2: transactional SQLite ControlBus (unchanged API) + one Discord ingestion authority with explicit fallback
portfolio.problem: ALL VERIFIED in platform_core/runtime/control.py: the sidecar lock proceeds 'best-effort WITHOUT the lock' on timeout (line 94); the corrupt-rebuild path resets data={} (lines 211-217), silently zeroing the autonomy_spent_usd financial ledger whose monotonicity autonomy_allowance.py promises; clear() (line 314-315) writes _blank() with NO locking — the exact bug class clearForRunStart was written to fix; pushOp's identity dedup (lines 285-294, with an in-code confession) exists ONLY because two live ingestion paths — the gateway bot's on_message AND the orchestrator's in-run REST poller (control_mixin.py:40 _translateDiscord, called from 5 sites incl. execute_mixin.py:293) — parse the SAME '!' messages; the dedup also swallows a user legitimately typing !retry twice, while !add/!inject/!deadline still double-apply if pushes straddle a drain. ~180 of control.py's 330 lines are hand-rolled concurrency that still cannot serialize two bypassing processes; three separate sleep-poll gate loops duplicate the same wait machinery.
portfolio.design: (1) New platform_core/runtime/control_store.py: SQLite state/control.db (WAL, busy_timeout=30000). Tables: flags(task_id, key, value, updated_at, PK(task_id,key)) for abort/pause/kill_subprocess/force_replan/pending_gate/seen_discord_id; decisions(task_id, gate, verdict, decided_at, PK(task_id,gate)); ops(id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, task_id, op_json, source_msg_id, created_at, UNIQUE(task_id, source_msg_id)); ledger(task_id, attempt_id UNIQUE, usd, at). ControlBus in control.py keeps its EXACT public API; each method is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction on a per-call connection — delete _fileLock, _atomicReplace, _readRaw, _CorruptBus, _PROCESS_LOCK, retry ladders, strict/tolerant modes, identity dedup. drainOps = 'DELETE FROM ops WHERE task_id=? RETURNING op_json' ordered by id (sqlite >=3.35; stdlib on Py3.11 ships it). autonomy_allowance.meterSpend(attempt_id, usd) = INSERT OR IGNORE; spent() = SELECT COALESCE(SUM(usd),0) — idempotency and monotonicity structural; mailbox corruption can no longer zero money. clearForRunStart deletes only ops+seen+pending_gate rows in one transaction; clear() is transactional too. One-shot migration reads any existing state/control/*.json. (2) Ingestion authority (lens B's design wins over lens C's outright poller delete — the abort channel must survive bot death mid-run): the gateway bot is the owner; control_mixin._translateDiscord polls ONLY when not isBotAlive() (heartbeat from R9, or a standalone state/heartbeats/gateway-bot.json written by the bot's existing presence loop if R9 hasn't landed); the degraded mode is logged once on transition. Every ingested command carries its Discord message id: commands.applyCommand passes source_msg_id into bus.pushOp(op, source_msg_id=...) — one message ingested twice is one op, two identical user messages are two ops. (3) One bus.waitDecision(gate, timeout, poll=1.0) helper encapsulating pause/abort/night-mode escapes replaces the three sleep-poll gate loops (~120 lines).
portfolio.test_strategy: test_control_concurrency/test_fuzz_control rewritten against the same public API from N threads; NEW true cross-process test via multiprocessing spawn (3 processes x 200 interleaved requestAbort/pushOp/drainOps — no op lost or duplicated, abort always visible); ledger idempotency (same attempt_id twice = one charge); kill a writer subprocess mid-transaction -> db intact (WAL); poller gating: fresh bot heartbeat -> zero REST calls (mock requests), stale -> polls; waitDecision matrix (decision / abort / timeout / night-mode); dedup semantics: same source_msg_id from two 'processes' -> one op, two msg ids with identical body -> two ops.
portfolio.breaking_changes: state/control/*.json retired (one-shot migration). pushOp gains source_msg_id kwarg; whole-op identity dedup removed — '!retry twice' now retries twice (documented in command help). Tests patching control internals re-target the public API.

portfolio.title: Run lifecycle integrity: abort survives crashes, single-writer task state, one heartbeat liveness primitive, IPC out of the task-store namespace
portfolio.problem: Three compounding holes invert operator control on the recovery path: (a) run_phase_outcome.handleRunAbort calls setStatus/writeIndex/sendEmbed UNWRAPPED while sibling handleRunCrash wraps both — a failing save turns an ABORT into a 'crash'; (b) resilience.run_with_recovery never consults ControlBus.isAbort(), so that 'crash' is auto-RESUMED — the operator said stop and the system restarts the run; (c) resilience swallows reload_state failure with bare pass, so unreadable state after a crash burns the whole restart budget with zero diagnostics. Separately, state/tasks/<id>.json is mutated from three processes with only an in-process save lock: the bot process writes task JSON directly (stale cleanup, !mode), tunnel.py mutates state.meta from a daemon thread WITHOUT the state lock, and launchOrError has a check-then-spawn TOCTOU plus newest-file-polling launch confirmation. VERIFIED: state_epoch is stamped on every save (task_io.py:64) with ZERO production readers — dead coherence theater. CORRECTED vs lens B: work_launcher._isStale is already PID-authoritative (work_launcher.py:241-258); the mtime false-abort risk is real only for pidless/psutil-missing tasks — still worth unifying, but not the primary hazard. Also VERIFIED-adjacent: terminal_ipc puts terminal_nav.json/terminal_mirror.json inside the task store's glob namespace, so iterStored can misparse them.
portfolio.design: (1) Abort-safe recovery: at the top of every run_with_recovery iteration, if ControlBus(task_id).isAbort(): finalize partial with status='aborted' and return — the bus flag persists independently of task JSON, so operator intent survives any state-save failure. handleRunAbort wraps persistence and notification in separate try/excepts exactly like handleRunCrash (LOG.error on persistence failure). Replace the reload-state bare pass with LOG.warning(exc_info=True) + a 3-strike streak that finalizes with distinct reason 'state file unreadable: <err>'. main._resolveOrphan swallow gains one LOG.warning. (2) Single-writer rule enforced: only the orchestrator process writes task JSON. New platform_core/runtime/heartbeat.py: writeHeartbeat(task_id, pid, seq) atomic-replaces state/heartbeats/<task_id>.json every 10s from the run loop tick; isRunAlive(task_id, grace_s=45) = heartbeat fresh OR pid alive; also a gateway-bot heartbeat writer (isBotAlive) consumed by R8's poller gating. work_launcher._isStale becomes not isRunAlive(...) (mtime heuristic deleted); on stale it calls bus.requestAbort() + pushOp mark_stale and NEVER writes task JSON — a new task_io.reapDeadRun(task_id) (refuses unless isRunAlive is False) finalizes truly-dead runs. Bot-side mutations (!mode etc.) become queued plan_ops drained by the run loop. tunnel._announce receives the orchestrator's state_lock (same pattern dashboard.start uses). Launch: module Lock + O_EXCL state/launch/launching.lock; main.py takes --launch-id and writes state/launch/<id>.json at startup — the bot confirms via handshake, not newest-file polling. (3) Terminal IPC files move to state/ipc/ (paths from app_config.paths); iterStored validates shape (requires task_id + meta) and counts+logs skipped files. (4) Delete the state_epoch stamp and tests/test_coherence_invariant.py; document the single-writer rule in docs/STATE.md.
portfolio.test_strategy: test_resilience additions: run_fn raises + bus abort set -> status 'aborted', run_fn NOT re-invoked; reload_state raising 3x -> 'state file unreadable' terminal reason + caplog warnings; handleRunAbort with raising setStatus -> no propagation, embed still attempted. Heartbeat matrix (fresh/stale/pid-alive). work_launcher regression: heartbeat-alive run NOT reaped despite old task-file mtime. Double-launch: two concurrent launchOrError -> exactly one spawn (mock spawn). iterStored: a terminal_nav.json-shaped file in the store dir is skipped and counted, not crashed on. Grep-test: no state.save()/setStatus call sites remain under notifications/ (bot process).
portfolio.breaking_changes: Bot can no longer force task JSON directly — !mode applies at next drain tick (~seconds). state_epoch and its test deleted (dead mechanism). STATE_DIR gains sibling dirs heartbeats/, launch/, ipc/; anything hardcoding state/tasks/terminal_mirror.json (grep: only terminal_ipc) updates.

portfolio.title: Verification with one owner: typed Receipt pipeline, strict expect (no silent FAIL->PASS), diff-grounded checks, single verdict parser
portfolio.problem: 'Verified' is smeared across six mechanisms and the core is rotten. VERIFIED at agents/verifier_runner.py:205-206: 'if not passed and proc.returncode == 0 and _isTestRunner(cmd): passed = True' — the runner silently flips FAIL to PASS for test-runner-shaped commands, discarding the brain's authored expect (the in-code comment even rationalizes it). verifier.buildContentScanVerify certifies work by checking goal WORDS appear as tokens in the target file — a comment containing the words passes; its five patch annotations (FX-2/3/14/15, LIVE BUG #2b) document whack-a-mole on a fragile proxy. adversary_review.review() inlines a byte-for-byte duplicate of _parseVerdict (~lines 248-269 vs 207-228) so the fail-closed parse can drift; _COMPOUND_PREFIXES is defined twice (verifier.py, verifier_runner.py); sanitization is applied at call sites instead of inside the runner. The repo's own rule says the verifier OWNS verification status — ownership is fiction today.
portfolio.design: New agents/verification.py owning the pipeline; verifier/verifier_runner shrink to internals. Core type: frozen dataclass Receipt(verdict: Verdict enum PASS/FAIL/ERROR/SKIPPED, cmd: list[str], rc, expect_mode, matched, missing, diff_files, duration_s, failure_feedback, annotations: dict) — envelope self-report, independent-verifier verdict, and adversary verdict become ANNOTATIONS on the one receipt, never verdict overrides. Pipeline, strictly ordered: (a) sanitize MANDATORY inside runVerification (delete call-site sanitize), execute the acceptance command as an arg-vector (no shell) through the existing tree-kill runner with cancel_check; (b) evaluate expect STRICTLY — delete the 205-206 override; update plan_mixin's VERIFY RULES prompt in the SAME patch so the brain authors exit_zero for test runners, and make the plan sanitizer reject a missing expect instead of the runner guessing; (c) replace buildContentScanVerify with diff-grounded evaluation: git diff --name-only must intersect the subtask's declared target files AND the acceptance command must reference at least one changed file — the token-scan synthesizer and its FX patch trail are deleted; (d) independent verify and adversary review become optional pipeline stages populating Receipt fields; evidence_gate/evidence_receipt fold in as ~40-line stages reading Receipt.diff_files instead of recomputing. Dedup: adversary_review.review() calls the one _parseVerdict; one _COMPOUND_PREFIXES lives in verification.py. Execute seam consumes Receipt.passed + failure_feedback via a dict-style/.passed compat shim for one release (independently landable without R-typed-outcomes).
portfolio.test_strategy: Characterization FIRST: capture current verify outcomes for the SimBrain dry-run suite (test_dry_run.py) and assert Receipt reproduces them EXCEPT the two intentional strictness changes, which get dedicated regressions: (1) test-runner cmd, rc==0, expect stdout_contains('X') absent -> FAIL (was PASS); (2) goal-word inside a comment no longer passes; (3) unchanged declared-target file -> FAIL with actionable feedback. Fail-closed verdict parse: garbled adversary output -> CHALLENGED via the single _parseVerdict (property test over the two previously-diverging paths). Receipt.verdict is a pure function of (rc, output, expect) — no cmd-shape special cases.
portfolio.breaking_changes: Verification gets STRICTER: plans relying on the test-runner override or token-scan will FAIL until replans author real expects — the VERIFY RULES prompt change ships in the same patch (SimBrain fixtures updated accordingly). vresult dict shape replaced by Receipt behind a compat shim for one release.

portfolio.title: Crash-safe IO kernel in platform_core/core: fsio + jsonl_io + clock + git_io — delete ~20 hand copies, fix the jq/PR-review live bug
portfolio.problem: Four infrastructure rituals are copy-pasted 5-9x each with drift and live bugs. Atomic write: task_io.py and control.py carry byte-identical temp+replace+Windows-backoff code (task_io.py:71 confesses 'Mirrors ControlBus._write'); VERIFIED trajectory.py:84-92 rewrites the ENTIRE span list per span with a FIXED temp name (path.with_suffix('.json.tmp')) — the exact race the unique-temp discipline exists to prevent, plus O(n^2) IO while claiming append-only. JSONL append/tail is re-implemented ~8x (audit.py the only copy with rotation); adversary_trust parses all lines in ONE try so a single torn line erases the whole trust history. Elapsed/ISO-clock formatting exists 6-7x (cv2.py admits 'mirror dashboard's, kept local to avoid a cycle'). Git subprocess wrappers exist 9x with divergent safety flags — worktree.py has NO timeout, so a credential prompt hangs a run. LIVE BUG VERIFIED at pr_feedback.py:159-161: gh is invoked with jq '.[].{state,body}' — invalid jq syntax — so the call always fails and PR review state ALWAYS degrades to 'none' (line 162-164): promote_safe silently reflects CI only.
portfolio.design: Four new stdlib-only leaf modules in the EXISTING platform_core/core package: (1) fsio.py — atomicWriteText(path, text, retries=8, backoff=0.02, cap=0.4), atomicWriteJson, loadJson(path, default), updateJson(path, mutate_fn, lock=False) keeping a .bak of last-good on corrupt read + WARNING instead of silent reset, fileLock(path, stale_after, timeout) writing owner pid and stealing only after re-stat confirms the same lock (fixes the remove-fresh-lock race) — unique pid-thread-rand temp names throughout. (2) jsonl_io.py — appendRecord(path, record, max_bytes=None) with rotation, iterRecords(path) with per-line try/except returning (records, skipped_count), readTail(path, n). (3) clock.py — nowIsoUtc/nowIsoLocal/parseIso/elapsedSecondsSince/fmtElapsed + RunClock(deadline_at) replacing the resilience.py + run_loop.py duplicate deadline math (alias-first timestamp canonicalization to avoid comparison breaks). Ports (behavior-preserving): task_io.save; trajectory becomes genuinely append-only JSONL (one open/close event per line, O(1) per event; reader reconstructs the span tree and accepts old .json for one release); obsidian, audit, user_prefs, sie/selfplay state files, adversary_trust (torn lines no longer erase history), dashboard/cv2 import fmtElapsed, the 9 git wrappers, and pr_feedback (_gh ported, jq fixed to '.[] | {state, body}', its 55-line _selfTest + sys.path hack deleted). EXPLICITLY OUT of scope to avoid cross-item conflicts: control.py (R8 replaces its storage), terminal_ipc.py (R9 relocates it), app_config env-coercion + knowledge_refresh (R12 owns app_config/config layering), LLM client (R5).
portfolio.test_strategy: Kernel unit suite: concurrent atomicWrite from 8 threads + 2 processes on Windows (no FileNotFoundError/torn file); updateJson corrupt input -> .bak preserved + warning; iterRecords with torn tail -> N-1 records + skipped_count=1 (adversary_trust regression); fileLock steal race; runGit timeout kills a hung child; RunClock edge at deadline. Trajectory property test: replaying the JSONL reconstructs the same span tree the old writer produced. pr_feedback: unit test with canned gh JSON asserts review state parses to approved/changes_requested (regression: previously always 'none'). All existing per-store tests pass unchanged (behavior-preserving ports).

portfolio.title: Config v2: one env bootstrap, typed registry behind a PEP 562 facade, PROJECT_ROOT landmine defused
portfolio.problem: VERIFIED at platform_core/app_config/paths.py:47: PROJECT_ROOT defaults to the app_config package's own directory ('_envPath("PROJECT_ROOT", str(_THIS_DIR)) or _THIS_DIR') — with the env var unset, STATE_DIR/LOG_PATH/EXPERIENCE_DB_PATH resolve INSIDE platform_core/app_config/; it is masked only because root config.py loads .env first. The '... or default' fallbacks are unreachable dead branches. Three load_dotenv calls point at a nonexistent package-local .env, so env works only if root config imports first. set_override mutates config's globals() ONLY, so config.KNOB and platform_core.app_config.llm.KNOB silently diverge after a live-tune and derived constants never update. Star-imports with no __all__ pollute the namespace (config.os exists) and blind type-checkers. VERIFIED: paths.py re-implements _envBool/_envInt (lines 30-43) despite _env.py being the declared single home; llm.py is a 421-line junk drawer (Obsidian, git timeouts, self-mod boundaries, prompt constants) and llm_epic_flags.py exists solely to duck the 450-line threshold.
portfolio.design: (1) Bootstrap in _env.py: locateRepoRoot() walks up from __file__ to a .git/pyproject marker; loadEnvOnce() idempotent, trying INSTALL_ROOT/.env then repo-root/.env; PROJECT_ROOT default = the computed repo root, never _THIS_DIR. Delete the three dead load_dotenv calls, the unreachable 'or default' fallbacks, and the duplicated _envBool/_envInt (single-homed in _env.py). (2) Typed registry: frozen dataclasses per domain (PathsCfg, OllamaCfg, ClaudeCliCfg, DiscordCfg, SieCfg, EpicFlags, PromptsCfg) built by one buildSettings() layering coded defaults < .env < sie_overrides.json — overrides become a first-class layer instead of post-hoc globals() surgery; module-level singleton with reload() for tests. (3) Facade: config.py keeps 100% backward name-compat via module __getattr__ (PEP 562) delegating to the live registry — config.MAX_SUBTASK_ATTEMPTS always reflects overrides; set_override writes registry + persists sie_overrides.json atomically (via R4's fsio); explicit __all__; _envInt/_envFloat kept as thin re-exports for tests. Run-scoped flags main.py currently pokes into config globals (NIGHT_MODE, WEB_DASHBOARD_PORT, CLAUDE_DOC_FETCH) move to explicit parameters/TaskState.meta — main.py stops mutating config. (4) llm.py contents reorganized into the domain dataclasses; llm_epic_flags.py deleted (fields become EpicFlags, names re-exported). Direction rule: platform_core.knowledge_base modules import platform_core.app_config directly, never root config (fixes the layering inversion in scraper/builder/compress/knowledge_refresh). Runs AFTER R3 so the HN_* group is already gone.
portfolio.test_strategy: NEW: import platform_core.app_config.paths in a subprocess with PROJECT_ROOT unset and assert it equals the repo root (landmine regression); set_override then assert config.X AND the registry field both changed (divergence regression); existing config tests pass via __getattr__ compat; full fast lane + test_dry_run (heaviest config consumer). Grep gates: 'load_dotenv' appears exactly once; 'globals()[' zero hits in config.py; NO model/effort-routing knob changes values (assert defaults byte-identical pre/post).
portfolio.breaking_changes: 'from config import X' still works but snapshots at import time (unchanged from today — documented). config namespace loses accidental exports (config.os, config.Path). platform_core no longer imports root config (import-order side effects change; conftest already isolates).

portfolio.title: best_effort() degradation kernel: counted, logged, surfaced — plus a log-level knob and rotation
portfolio.problem: Hundreds of 'except Exception' swallow sites (pervasive across platform_core/orchestration, notifications, memory — grep hits capped out during verification) implement 'never break the run' as universal silence: Obsidian down, tunnel dead, narration lost, ledger writes failing 100%, jerry dataset truncation all look identical — nothing. VERIFIED at config.py:152-167: logging is hardcoded to INFO with a single unrotated FileHandler and no env knob, so every LOG.debug failure diagnostic in the codebase is permanently unreachable for a system running 8-hour autonomous loops. The FX-9 'degraded run' check has to string-match reason text because no structured degradation data exists.
portfolio.design: New platform_core/core/best_effort.py: @contextmanager best_effort(name, *, log=None, level=WARNING) — swallows Exception, logs full traceback at DEBUG, emits ONE WARNING per (name, exc_type) per process (dedup dict), and increments a module-level DEGRADATIONS registry {name: {count, last_error, last_at}}. degradationSummary() consumed by: run teardown (one aggregated 'degraded surfaces: obsidian x12, tunnel x1' line in the final embed), platform_core/ops/doctor.py, and webdash /api/state. The experience-ledger swallow pattern routes through it with per-table names ('ledger.subtasks'), yielding ledger_health() for free — this absorbs the observability half of the deferred ledger rewrite. Logging: _configureLogging reads NINE_TO_FIVE_LOG_LEVEL (default INFO) and switches to RotatingFileHandler(10MB, backupCount=5). Migration is mechanical and incremental: convert the top ~80 highest-value sites this session (run_phase_mixin, control_mixin, resilience, jerry_client, hooks_obsidian, memory/experience_schema, dashboard) and add a dev.py ratchet counting remaining bare 'except Exception: pass' sites against a recorded baseline. Runs LAST (wave 4) so it never instruments code another item deletes and layers cleanly on R12's config and R8's control_mixin.
portfolio.test_strategy: Unit: best_effort swallows, counts, dedups (caplog: 1 WARNING for 100 identical failures, count=100 in registry); degradationSummary shape; NINE_TO_FIVE_LOG_LEVEL override; rotation smoke. Integration: simulator run with a raising Obsidian stub -> run completes AND final summary contains the degraded-surfaces line. Ratchet test asserting bare-swallow count <= recorded baseline.

portfolio.title: One LLM client + explicit act tag: sim doubles dispatch on structured metadata, never prompt wording

Any prompt rewording (R10 changes the VERIFY RULES prompt this very session) keeps the dry-run green while exercising the WRONG code path. Feeding this fragility: the Ollama client + one-shot chat + retry loop is re-implemented in ~15 modules (verbatim _getOllama copies across agents/ and discovery/; human_nature's copies die in R3), and elaborator._chat still extracts with raw resp.get('message') — the exact pydantic-vs-dict bug class that already caused the production incident llm_io.responseText was created to fix (owner memory: ollama-empty-completion-debug).
portfolio.design: (1) llm_io.py grows chat(system, user, *, act: str, model=None, want_json=False, retries=3, client=None) owning the memoized client (host/num_ctx/keep_alive constant per the incident learnings), the single blessed retry/backoff, empty-completion salvage, and responseText/responseJson extraction; parseJsonLoose(text) promoted from brain_io.parseJsonText (the most complete ladder), with adversary_review._loadJsonLoose and responseJson delegating to it. (2) The act tag ('architect'|'plan'|'critique'|'invocation_spec'|'replan'|'gatekeeper'|'compaction'|...) is threaded through the orchestrator brain seam (llm_mixin._ollamaChat / brain_io) as structured metadata: real Ollama ignores it; SimBrain/BuilderBrain dispatch on it EXACTLY, and an unknown act RAISES in sim (fail loud) — prompt rewording can no longer silently redirect the sim. The act tag is recorded on trajectory spans for free telemetry. (3) Delete the surviving _getOllama copies and elaborator's raw extraction/retry loop; elaborator/architect/replanner/lenses/synthesis become pure prompt builders taking an injectable chat callable (clarifier already has this shape). NO model or effort routing changes — model selection stays exactly where it is. Runs before R10 in its wave chain (shares adversary_review.py; R10's prompt edit then lands against act-dispatch, proving the mechanism).
portfolio.test_strategy: test_dry_run + test_builder_sim green with act-dispatch. Unknown act in sim raises. llm_io.chat pydantic-object vs dict extraction parity (extend test_llm_io_pydantic.py). parseJsonLoose golden cases merged from the three existing implementations. Grep gate: '_getOllama' appears zero times outside llm_io.
